QueryApi.FieldMapping.title: QueryApi.FieldMapping
QueryApi.FieldMapping.description: Describes a mapping for an input field to its new name and other properties Auto-generated example JSON

name.description: The name of the output field. Field names are case insensitive but preserving, and cannot have leading or trailing whitespace.

inputField.description: The name of the input field. Field names are case insensitive but preserving, and cannot have leading or trailing whitespace.

customOrder.description:
Set a custom order to be applied when sorting by the field.
Values not present in this list, but present in the data will be set after any of the specified value following the natural order.
Values present in this list, but not present in the data will be ignored.
If a custom order is already defined for this field, This will take precedence.If null, the natural order will be applied when sorting by the output field (if no custom order already exists for the field).
Custom order cannot be defined on range fields.

formatting.description:
The formatting options for the output field.
If not null, this will override any any existing formatting options associated to the field.
Formatting options will be propagated troughout the query dag, and they will instruct the client o how o format the field value.

QueryApi.FieldMappingOperation.title: QueryApi.FieldMappingOperation
QueryApi.FieldMappingOperation.description: Describes a single layer within a query for mapping fields to include in the result. Field order in output will be: (1) mapping fields; (2) other input fields, if includeAllInputFields=true Auto-generated example JSON

mappings.description: The list of field mappings to include in the result. They are applied in order as defined.

includeAllInputFields.description:
If false (default) it will only include the fields defined in the mappings. If true it will include all input fields not otherwise selected. The field order will be preserved and fields will be added after any mapping. If any input field omitted from mappings conflicts with a new field added with the same name, it will be invalid.
Example: true

variables.description: The list of formula variable values that are available for use within formula fields.

input.description: The single input to this operation. Optional. For example, a SimpleQuery.

comment.description: A comment string associated to the query. A comment will have no effect on the query result and it is meant a human readable explanation of what the query purpose is.

QueryApi.Filter.title: QueryApi.Filter
QueryApi.Filter.description: Describes a single constraint (or a group of constraints with logical combination), equivalent to an SQL WHERE clause item. Auto-generated example JSON

inputField.description:
Relevant when #type is FIELD_VALUE only. The name of the input field. Field names are case insensitive but preserving, and cannot have leading or trailing whitespace.
Aliases: field

operator.description: Relevant when #type is FIELD_VALUE only. Default EQUALS. Note that operators such as ">=" implicitly exclude NULL values.

value.description:
Relevant when #type is FIELD_VALUE only. The value to compare against, or for #operator IN, an array of values. Can be null for "EQUALS null" rule, or an array containing null for "IN (..., null, ...)" rule. Note that (e.g.) EQUALS(42) will match only 42 and will implicitly exclude all nulls; likewise NOT(EQUALS(42)) will match only 'not 42' so will implicitly include nulls and all other numbers. ValueRange objects can be used here to provide minumum and maximum bounds. Long values greater than 2^53 can be written as String to maintain precision.
Aliases: values

filters.description:
Relevant when #type is AND, OR or NOT. The nested filters to combine in an AND or OR rule (can be empty for FULL or NONE selections respectively), or a single nested filter for a NOT rule.
Aliases: filter

geoDistance.description: Relevant when #type is GEO_DISTANCE only. The geographic-distance payload containing the coordinate field references, centre point, and maximum distance in kilometres.

end.description:

QueryApi.FormulaQueryInput.title: QueryApi.FormulaQueryInput
QueryApi.FormulaQueryInput.description: Request body for the /formula endpoint. Defines the configuration of a formula expression evaluation request. Auto-generated example JSON

input.description: The single input to this operation. Optional. For example, a SimpleQuery.

formulas.description: The formulas to evaluate. This should be in the Omniscope formula syntax, which is similar to Excel formulae, with field references in [square brackets], e.g. SUBSET_SUM([a]) / 3. See https://help.visokio.com/support/solutions/articles/42000111298-functions-and-formulae-in-omniscope for a list of Omniscope formula functions, however not all are supported here. Note, unlike classic, zero-arg function names must always be followed by brackets, e.g. RAND().

variables.description: The list of formula variable values that are available for use within the formula.

comment.description: A comment string associated to the query. A comment will have no effect on the query result and it is meant a human readable explanation of what the query purpose is.

QueryApi.GeoDistanceFilter.title: QueryApi.GeoDistanceFilter
QueryApi.GeoDistanceFilter.description: Geographic distance payload for {@link FilterType#GEO_DISTANCE} filters. Records must have their coordinate value within {@link #maxDistanceKm} kilometres of ({@link #centreLatitude}, {@link #centreLongitude }) as measured by the Spherical Law of Cosines. Auto-generated example JSON

latField.description: Schema field containing the record's latitude in decimal degrees.

lonField.description: Schema field containing the record's longitude in decimal degrees.

centreLatitude.description:
Centre point latitude in decimal degrees (valid range [-90, 90]).
Example: 123.45

centreLongitude.description:
Centre point longitude in decimal degrees (valid range [-180, 180]).
Example: 123.45

maxDistanceKm.description:
Maximum distance in kilometres (inclusive, must be >= 0). A value of 0 matches only records at the exact centre point.
Example: 123.45

QueryApi.Grouping.title: QueryApi.Grouping
QueryApi.Grouping.description: Describes a single level/tier of grouping, similar an SQL GROUP BY condition or Omniscope "Bar" view's 'Split' option. Auto-generated example JSON

inputField.description:
The name of the input field. Field names are case insensitive but preserving, and cannot have leading or trailing whitespace.
Aliases: field

type.description: The method for bucketing/grouping the data. UNIQUE_VALUES is comparable to GROUP BY in SQL.

dateUnit.description:
Relevant when #type is HISTOGRAM and #inputField is a date type.
If the input field has some formatting options, these will be amended to drop no longer significant sections.
If the input field does not have formatting options, a new date formatting will be introduced with pattern 'yyyy-MM-dd hh:mm:ss'
 dropped to the unit specified.
For example, if the input field does not have a formatting and we are grouping by hour, the 
 output field will have a date formatting options with pattern  dd/MM/yyyy HH

histogramInterval.description:
Required when #type is HISTOGRAM. The width of each histogram interval. For DATE fields, must be integer and also factors of 60 (for minutes/seconds), 24 (hours), 12 (months), precisely 1 (days), or any integer (years).
Example: 123.45

name.description: The name of the output field. Field names are case insensitive but preserving, and cannot have leading or trailing whitespace.

QueryApi.JoinOperation.title: QueryApi.JoinOperation
QueryApi.JoinOperation.description: Describes a single layer within a query for joining two inputs into one. Field order in output will be: (1) source field (if any); (2) common fields in criteria; (3) left fields not in criteria; (4) right fields not in criteria.If right fields non in criteria have the same name as a left field non in criteria, right fields will be renamed with the original name followed by a space and integer number (e.g., 'A', 'A 2', 'A 3' (if 'A 2' is already a left field)). Auto-generated example JSON

left.description: The left input to the join. For example, a SimpleQuery.

right.description: The right input to the join. For example, a SimpleQuery.

criteria.description: The list of criteria to apply.

leftMismatches.description:
Include left input mismatches in the result. False by default
Example: true

matches.description:
Include matches in the result. True by default
Example: true

rightMismatches.description:
Include right input mismatches in the result. False by default
Example: true

sourceFieldName.description:
Name of the optional source field. If populated, this will be a new field whose values indicate the table where records come from.
If the values of the criteria fields are only present in the left input, this will be set to Left
If the values of the criteria fields are only present in the right input this will be set to Right
If the values of the criteria fields are present in both left and right input this will be set to Left, Right
The field must be named in a way that it does not collide with any of the output fields.

comment.description: A comment string associated to the query. A comment will have no effect on the query result and it is meant a human readable explanation of what the query purpose is.

QueryApi.Measure.title: QueryApi.Measure
QueryApi.Measure.description: Describes how to roll up numeric/date data, thereby producing an additional aggregated column in the output. Auto-generated example JSON

name.description:
The name of the output field. Field names are case insensitive but preserving, and cannot have leading or trailing whitespace.
If left unspecified a default name will be assigned as the name of the input field followed by the name of the function between parenthesis. It is a good practice to not, rely on this automatic name generation but use an explicit name where necessary

inputField.description:
Relevant when #function is a field-specific function such as SUM, MIN, MEAN. The name of the input field. Field names are case insensitive but preserving, and cannot have leading or trailing whitespace.
Aliases: field

weightField.description: Relevant when #function is {@link MeasureFunction#MEAN} to specify a weighted mean.

function.description: The aggregation function to roll up a series of values.

percentileValue.description:
Must be populated if and only if the function is PERCENTILE. If populated its value must be between 0 and 100 inclusive.
+The result of the measure will be the value of the field below which a this percentage of values will fall.
For example, if set to 20, the result of the measure will be the value below which 20% of the field values are found
Example: 123.45

formula.description: Relevant when #function is FORMULA only. The formula itself, such as `SUBSET_SUM([a]) / SUBSET_MEAN([b])`.
